title: Exponential queue attenuator and fast repave automation for GPU exhaustion follow-up
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: During the 2026-03 hosted GPU exhaustion event we observed sustained queue amplification from a small set of tenants that triggered autoscaler hysteresis and prolonged throttling. Root causes: (1) tenant workloads with large KV-cache churn and long-tail sequences caused steady per-tenant queue growth; (2) autoscaler hysteresis and slow prewarm left pools under-provisioned for ~7 minutes; (3) a small number of worker VMs exhibited progressive GPU memory leak (driver/kernel-level) that reduced effective capacity. Proposal: implement a two-pronged mitigation: (A) an "exponential queue attenuator" — a lightweight, probabilistic admission controller that reduces queue input for tenants exhibiting queue growth using an exponential drop factor tied to tail P95/P99 queue latency; (B) "fast repave automation" — an automated node health monitor that detects stuck GPU memory usage and replaces affected workers automatically while coordinating graceful request drain.
acceptance_criteria: Median queue length during simulated tenant spike reduced by >= 40% in staging compared to current baseline
P95 request admission latency improved by >= 30% under synthetic surge load
Incident recovery time (time to return to healthy pool utilization) reduced from ~7 minutes to <= 2 minutes in simulated runs with fast repave enabled
No customer-facing 5xx regression in canary rollout (0 errors attributable to attenuator for 48h)
Operational runbook updated and on-call engineer can trigger/disable attenuator within 5 minutes

comments: 2026-03-10 - Asha Patel: Postmortem summary attached to the incident channel. Recommending short-term guardrails plus long-term autoscaler tuning. Starting design work on attenuator.

2026-03-11 - Liam Chen: Initial design sketch complete. Exponential drop factor proposed: drop_prob = 1 - exp(-alpha * (q_score - baseline)), where q_score is a weighted P95/P99 latency. Chose alpha=0.12 for initial sim.

2026-03-11 - Ben Rosario: Telemetry plan: add metrics gpu_pool.queue_length_by_tenant, admission.drop_rate_by_tenant, attenuator.q_score. Dashboard prototype: https://console.redwood/internal/dashboards/gpu-attenuator

2026-03-11 - Priya Gupta: Fast repave criteria: GPU memory reserved > 92% for 5 minutes OR sustained CUDA OOM errors observed -> cordon + drain + spin replacement. Replacement template uses pre-warmed image to reduce bootstrap to ~60s. Implementation PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/pr/12891

2026-03-12 - Maya Singh: Prototype in admission-proxy branch 'exp-attenuator' passed synthetic tenant spike test (staging). Observed queue length down 48% and P95 down 34%. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/pr/12947

2026-03-12 - SRE (notes): Need to validate interactions with existing fair-share admission scoring — added a fairness floor so attenuator never reduces below 10% of baseline for tenants with paid reservations.

2026-03-12 - Product review (Sofia Martinez): Approved P0 and schedule for canary after docs and telemetry landed. Product asked for customer impact statement for enterprise tenants; ensured feature respects reservations and SLA tiers.
2026-03-12 - Action item: run 50 randomized simulation runs with different tenant mixes and attach results to the design doc before canary. Assigned to SRE.
notes: Design trade-offs: aggressive global drop could mask noisy neighbor effects but harm reserved customers — mitigated by reservation floor and priority exemption list. Fast repave has cost implications (recreate VMs) but reduces mean-time-to-recover vs manual operator fix. Tunables will be exposed as config flags per pool. We will also iterate alpha and thresholds in controlled experiments.
